answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 58% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the vertex quorum in the velvet ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the wander history publishes each cut. A farm that captures 124 seats therefore pays for 124 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 9 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
